title: MCP Ecosystem in 2026
content:
## Overview

The **Model Context Protocol (MCP)**, released by Anthropic in November 2024, has grown from a developer preview into the dominant open standard for connecting AI models to external tools and services. By mid-2026 the ecosystem spans ~13,000 servers, carries ~97 million monthly SDK downloads, and has achieved production adoption at 41% of surveyed software organizations.

---

## Growth at a Glance

| Metric | Mid-2025 | Mid-2026 |
|---|---|---|
| Official registry servers | ~200 | 800+ |
| Total servers (incl. community/private) | Hundreds | ~13,000 |
| Monthly SDK downloads | — | ~97 million |
| Org production adoption | — | 41% |
| AI platforms with native support | 1 (Anthropic) | 5+ |

---

## Platform Support

MCP support is no longer unique to Anthropic's stack. By 2026 every major AI platform ships native MCP client support:

- **Anthropic** — Claude API, Claude.ai, Claude Code
- **OpenAI** — ChatGPT, Assistants API
- **Google** — Gemini, Vertex AI Agent Builder
- **Microsoft** — GitHub Copilot, Azure AI Foundry
- **IDE tools** — Cursor, Windsurf, Zed (all ship built-in MCP clients)

---

## Community Servers by Category

Community-built servers cover virtually every developer and enterprise workflow:

| Category | Examples |
|---|---|
| Developer tools | GitHub, GitLab, Jira, Linear, Sentry |
| Databases | PostgreSQL, MySQL, MongoDB, Redis, Snowflake |
| Infrastructure | Docker, Kubernetes, AWS, GCP, Terraform |
| Communication | Slack, Notion, Google Drive, Gmail, Calendar |
| Payments | Stripe, Shopify |
| Design | Figma, Canva |
| Search & retrieval | Brave Search, Exa, Tavily |

---

## Governance: Linux Foundation

In early 2026, the MCP specification moved under the **Linux Foundation** for neutral, multi-stakeholder governance — analogous to how the OpenAPI Specification is maintained independently of Swagger/SmartBear. This formalized MCP's transition from "Anthropic's protocol" to an industry-owned standard.

The first **MCP Dev Summit North America** (April 2–3, 2026, New York City) featured 95+ sessions from Anthropic, OpenAI, Microsoft, Docker, and Bloomberg — marking the community's shift to institutional governance.

---

## Protocol Version: MCP v1.27

MCP v1.27 (April 2026) introduced three major capabilities:

- **Streaming tool results** — servers can push partial results as they arrive rather than waiting for completion, important for long-running database queries or file reads
- **Server-side tool filtering** — servers dynamically expose different tool subsets based on the authenticated user's permissions
- **OAuth 2.1 support** — standardized authentication flow for remote (HTTP/SSE) MCP servers, replacing the ad-hoc token schemes common in earlier implementations

---

## Enterprise MCP: Managed Agents

Claude's **Managed Agents** feature (2026) integrates directly with enterprise MCP deployments. Agents can:

- Run on a schedule (cron-based) with vault-stored credentials
- Connect to private MCP servers behind a corporate firewall
- Operate within a customer-controlled sandbox where both the execution environment and the services it reaches stay within established security boundaries

Anthropic separately released 20+ MCP connectors for legal workflows covering research, contracts, discovery, matter management, and legal aid.

---

## Security Considerations

With 13,000+ community servers, supply chain risk has become a significant concern:

- **Prompt injection via tool descriptions** — malicious servers can try to override Claude's instructions through tool `description` fields
- **Tool name collisions** — two servers can expose a tool with the same name, causing unpredictable routing
- **Dependency trust** — many community servers wrap third-party npm/PyPI packages with their own vulnerabilities

Anthropic's MCP client (Claude Code) validates tool descriptions and issues a warning before connecting to unverified servers. Third-party scanners (e.g., Stacklok's MCP security scanner) audit server packages for known vulnerabilities and injection patterns.
